authority: HM Land Registry GOV.UK practice guides
verified_contracts: registered title boundaries are normally general boundaries rather than exact legal lines
a determined boundary is recorded only after the exact line has been identified and then made apparent in the register
HM Land Registry does not resolve a boundary dispute merely by determining a boundary
the property register of each affected title records that a boundary is determined
title plans show the general position and may use lettered points for the determined extent
a filed determined-boundary plan is retained to identify the exact line
determined-boundary plans must clearly show start, end and turning points
supporting plans must contain enough surrounding detail to relate the line to Ordnance Survey mapping
plans must be drawn to a stated scale, with 1:200 preferred as a minimum practical scale
the current practice guides were updated on 1 June 2026

candidate_gate.reason: general-boundary and determined-boundary semantics verified but candidate-specific register and polygon evidence remains absent
